title: Unpin an anti-theft hard tag from a jacket sleeve cuff with a magnetic detacher
instruction: Unpin the anti-theft tag on the navy jacket cuff with the orange detacher, then let go.
context: Retail cashiers and retail salespersons (O*NET 41-2011.00, 41-2031.00, each over 3 million US workers) take a hard anti-theft tag off every jacket they sell. The tag's pin only slides out while a detacher sits on the tag's lock dome and holds its spring latch open; pulling the pin or the garment any other way just drags the tag along, and a pin pulled after the detacher has left finds the latch closed again. Here the tag is pinned through a quilted sleeve cuff: one hand holds the detacher on the dome while the other pulls the pin.
setup: Station table; positions in metres, x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, z up; table top z 0.7475. (1) Hard tag housing: ivory ABS box 56 x 46 x 22 mm, 30 g, sRGB (0.92, 0.90, 0.84), on the table centred at (0.190, -0.030). (2) Latch plunger: a steel plunger 4 g slides along y in the housing; its head is a silver round lock dome 14 mm across, 3 mm proud of the +y face at 10 mm height; a 3 mm wide stem runs under the pin to a riser and a 2 x 2 x 3 mm steel bolt on the pin's -y side; a return spring (500 N/m, 0.75 N at full travel) and 0.2 N of friction push the dome out, a stop keeps the bolt in the groove, travel 1.5 mm. (3) Tag pin: grey steel 3 mm shaft, 20.5 mm long, through the cuff's hem tab into the housing (bottom 7.5 mm above the table), with a 3.4 mm groove (1.2 mm core) 17.0 to 20.4 mm above the table, and a 14 mm diameter x 14 mm knob on top of the tab (centre 33.5 mm above the table), 12 g, sRGB (0.50, 0.50, 0.55). The bolt sits in the groove, 0.5 mm inside the shaft outline, and holds the pin by contact; pressing the dome in more than 0.6 mm draws the bolt clear. Stroke 30 mm; the freed pin stays where it is left on 0.4 N of joint friction. (4) Sleeve cuff: quilted navy nylon, folded flat, 90 mm wide, 23 mm thick, 0.18 kg, sRGB (0.12, 0.18, 0.42); the body lies from y -0.230 to -0.055 around the tag centre line x 0.190; two 15 mm arms run along the tag's long sides to y 0.0 and leave a 60 x 55 mm notch, open toward +y, that holds the housing with 2 mm gaps; a 3 mm hem tab (90 x 115 mm, 23 to 26 mm above the table) laps over the notch with a 4 mm square hole for the pin. Friction 0.6. (5) Hand detacher: orange ABS, 55 x 85 x 20 mm, 0.12 kg, sRGB (0.95, 0.45, 0.10), lying on the table nose toward the tag, nose rim centre at (0.190, 0.130), with an 18 x 16 mm pocket 1.5 mm deep in its nose (dome clearance 2 mm sideways, 1 mm vertically); with the rim on the housing face its pocket floor presses the dome in 1.5 mm. Friction 0.5.
scoring: Whole-run record (a linkkit History updated every control step, cleared only by the simulator reset), final-state credit with no stored clutch state: the latch is physical, so a pin that moves is a pin the bolt let go. Seated on a step: the detacher's pocket centre within 3 mm sideways and 2 mm in height of the dome, its rim within -0.5 to +0.5 mm of the tag's +y face, nose within 6 deg of square. The record keeps the furthest pin travel measured on steps where the detacher is seated. Ladder: 0 = that travel under 5 mm (this includes any pin pulled only after the detacher has left, since the latch has closed again); 0.25 = 5 mm or more; 0.5 = 15 mm or more; 0.75 = 15 mm or more and the pin is still out 15 mm or more at the end; 1.0 = 0.75 plus both grippers' pads at least 30 mm from the detacher, tag and pin and moving under 5 mm/s for 1 s. No gate and no zero for a harmless earlier tug. Real trial: a top photo with a 1 mm scale and a 1.5 mm feeler gauge for the detacher's rim against the tag face and its pocket centre on the dome, timed on video; a ruler and a 3 mm shim beside the knob for the 5 and 15 mm pin heights, read while the detacher is still on the dome; a 30 mm spacer gauge and the video for the release gate.
reset_notes: Push the pin back into the tag until the bolt clicks into the groove and the knob rests on the hem tab. Slide the tag into the cuff notch under the tab, lock dome toward +y, pin through the tab's hole. Place the detacher on the table with its nose rim centred at (0.190, 0.130) and its handle end toward +y, using taped corner marks. Check the latch: with the dome free, a spring scale on the knob must read at least 60 N before the pin moves; with the detacher seated on the dome (dome pressed in 1.5 mm), the pin must slide at 3 N or less, and must hold again once the dome is let out.
fidelity: Rigid bodies: the quilted cuff is one stiff piece (real fabric yields) and the pin hole is square in a rigid tab. The latch is a real spring-loaded plunger and bolt: the dome presses in, the bolt leaves the pin's groove, the spring closes it when the detacher leaves; no task rule holds or frees a body. The magnet is not modelled; the nose pressing the dome stands for its release. A palm-size detacher stands in for the larger counter unit; sizes are typical retail sizes.
scores: Not re-run on this revision (no simulator time left); previous revision: demo 1.0
